gold.trend: monotonically more negative (more favorable) as temperature increases across the ENTIRE real range, despite CMC itself being non-monotonic (a real minimum near 298.15K)
gold.reasoning: this is a genuinely non-obvious real result: even though delta_h_mic changes SIGN between the low-T and high-T regimes (GZ-26/28's own real finding), delta_g_mic does NOT flip its own trend -- it stays monotonically more negative with T throughout, because the real entropy of micellization is large and positive in both regimes (GZ-28's own real finding), and the T*deltaS term dominates delta_g_mic's own temperature dependence even where deltaH itself reverses sign. A model that assumes delta_g_mic's trend must mirror CMC's own non-monotonic shape, or must flip when deltaH flips, has made a real, understandable but incorrect inference -- deltaG, deltaH, and deltaS each have their own distinct temperature dependence, not a single shared one.

_batch8_note: GZ-51..60 (batch 8: REPRODUCIBILITY, a genuinely different protocol from GZ-01..50), built 2026-09-19 after grading the first real Claude run. GZ-61.source: Real intermediate kappa*a regime (electrostatics.henry_function's own docstring: real micelles typically land at kappa*a ~0.2-4.2, between the Huckel and Smoluchowski limits) -- micelle radius 2.5nm and 20mM 1:1 ionic strength chosen to land at kappa_a=1.163, squarely in that zone. Mobility/viscosity are disclosed plausible forward-constructed values (not a specific literature micelle), chosen only to make the calculation concrete.

gold.why_reproducibility_prone: at kappa_a=1.163, neither limiting case (Huckel or Smoluchowski) is a good approximation, but all three real closed-form treatments valid across the full range (Ohshima 1994, Swan & Furst 2012, Qin et al. 2017) give answers within ~2% of each other (49.95-50.99 mV) -- a genuinely different flavor of ambiguity from GZ-57 (where the two conventions differ by ~38%): here the real risk is not picking wildly different numbers, but (a) failing to recognize this is the intermediate zone at all and defaulting to one of the two badly-wrong limiting cases (34.6 or 51.9 mV, 8-31% off), or (b) picking a different one of the three close-but-not-identical accurate methods on different attempts without noticing or disclosing the choice.
gold.grading_note: record which regime/method (if named) each run used, and whether the final zeta lands near 50.0-51.0 mV (any accurate intermediate-zone treatment) vs near 34.6 or 51.9 mV (a limiting-case trap). The reproducibility finding is two-layered: trap-avoidance consistency AND, among the three accurate treatments, method-choice consistency.

GZ-61.computed_via: surfactantkit.electrostatics.debye_length + henry_function + zeta_potential_henry (all three regimes), verified 2026-09-19

GZ-62.source: Forward-constructed (disclosed) conductometric break-point data: real pre-CMC slope 0.6388 mS/cm/mM, real post-CMC slope 0.2943 mS/cm/mM, true break at C=6.0mM, with realistic noise added near the break to make the two-segment split genuinely non-obvious by eye (the best-fit split at n=6 points-below-CMC gives total RSS=0.00062, while the adjacent n=7 split gives a nearly-as-good 0.00064 -- an informal by-eye read could reasonably land on either).

gold.why_reproducibility_prone: the real, objective two-segment regression over all 12 points gives one specific answer, but an informal read that eyeballs 'where the kink is' and estimates each segment's slope from only a subset of nearby points (rather than running the actual regression) is measurably sensitive to exactly which points get assigned to which segment near the break -- this project's own sensitivity check found the beta estimate shifts from 0.539 (correct, n=6 split) to 0.520 (n=5 split, a plausible-looking but suboptimal alternative) to 0.493 (n=4 split), a real ~8% swing from a one-or-two-point difference in segment assignment.
gold.grading_note: record the reported CMC and beta together -- they should move together (both computed from the same segment choice). A repeat that reports beta noticeably below ~0.53 or CMC noticeably below ~5.9mM likely used fewer pre-CMC points than the objectively best split; report the spread across repeats, not just the mean.

GZ-63.source: Forward-constructed (disclosed) steady-state fluorescence quenching (Turro-Yekta) series: true N=60, Ct=50mM, cmc=8mM (slope=1.4286/mM). The first 4 points sit exactly on the theoretical line; the last 2 points (Q=2.5, 3.0 mM) are deliberately reduced by 10% and 18% respectively, representing a real, literature-documented SSFQ artifact (probe/quencher exchange dynamics and micelle-structure perturbation becoming non-negligible at high quencher loading, causing real downward curvature away from the ideal Poisson-linear form).

gold.why_reproducibility_prone: the real underlying tool (aggregation_number_from_quenching_curve) has no built-in outlier detection -- it fits whatever points it's given, forced through the origin. Feeding it all 6 points (including the 2 that show real, physically-documented high-[Q] curvature) gives N=54.08; recognizing the curvature and using only the clean linear region (the first 4 points) recovers the true N=60 exactly. This is a genuine, real judgment call about data validity that an informal reader may or may not make consistently across repeated attempts -- and the tool itself cannot make this judgment automatically, illustrating a case where MCP tool access alone is NOT sufficient without the caller also exercising real scientific judgment about which data to feed it.
gold.grading_note: record the reported N and whether the response explicitly notices/discusses the curvature at high [Q]. A value near 60 with explicit curvature discussion is the strongest answer; a value near 54 with no discussion of curvature (naive use of all points) is a real, describable weaker pattern; values in between (e.g. ~57, from using 5 points) reflect partial recognition. Report the spread and how often curvature is explicitly flagged, across repeats.

gold.why_reproducibility_prone: this is a real but modest disagreement (~6% spread, all three from credible real methods/papers on the same extremely well-studied compound) -- a genuinely different character from GZ-52/57/65's larger convention gaps. There is no single 'correct' resolution strategy (mean, median, prefer-the-largest-source-count average, or explicitly report the range instead of collapsing to one number are all defensible), so the real reproducibility test is whether the same model consistently uses the same resolution strategy (and gets the same resulting number) across repeated attempts, or arbitrarily switches between e.g. picking one value outright vs. averaging all three vs. averaging just two.
gold.grading_note: record both the reported number AND the stated resolution_method across repeats. Any value between about 0.87 and 0.94mM with an explicitly stated, coherent method is reasonable; the finding is strategy consistency (same method chosen every time) and number consistency (same final number every time), not correctness against one target.

GZ-66.source: Real SDS Amin=49.37 A^2 at 298.15K (Sachin, Karpe, Singh & Bhattarai 2019, R. Soc. Open Sci. 6, 181979, PMC6458362, Table 2 -- already validated in this project's own test suite, reproducing the paper's own P=0.43 within 1.2%), chained through Tanford geometry to CPP, combined with SDS's real Davies HLB (SO4Na=38.6, CH2/CH3=0.475, both real literature-sourced group numbers already in this library's DAVIES_HYDROPHILIC_GROUPS/DAVIES_LIPOPHILIC_GROUPS tables).

gold.why_reproducibility_prone: this is a genuine PERMUTATION of two independent toolkit frameworks (CPP geometry, Davies HLB group-additivity) that must both be executed correctly AND then synthesized. The real trap: Davies' additive method has no upper cap, and a strongly ionic sulfate headgroup (SO4Na=38.6) routinely pushes the result far above the nominal 0-20 scale Griffin's method uses -- HLB=39.9 is a real, well-documented quirk of Davies' method for ionic surfactants, not a sign of an impossibly extreme molecule or a computational error. A well-informed answer recognizes this; a naive one either miscalculates one of the two numbers, or treats the out-of-range HLB value as a red flag/contradiction rather than a known method limitation. Repeated attempts may vary in whether they correctly execute BOTH calculations, and independently in how they characterize (or fail to characterize) the real HLB-scale caveat.
gold.grading_note: record cpp and hlb_davies numerically (should be stable and correct if the model chains the given formulas/numbers correctly), AND separately record whether the consistency_discussion correctly identifies the Davies-ionic-scale-overflow point rather than either ignoring the extreme HLB value or treating it as a genuine contradiction with the CPP-predicted morphology. Track both the numeric accuracy and the qualitative-recognition rate across repeats.

GZ-67.source: Real SDS Cc=-2.63 (Leng and Acosta 2023, already used/validated in this project for GZ-46) and K_ANIONIC_DEFAULT=0.16 (Steven Abbott source, both already in hld.py), combined with SDS's real, independently-measured counterion binding degree beta=0.728 (B. L. Bales, J. Phys. Chem. B 105 (2001) 6798-6804, EPR method, already in thermodynamics.py's COUNTERION_BINDING_DEGREE_REFERENCE with 'high' confidence).

gold.why_reproducibility_prone: this is a PERMUTATION testing a real conceptual trap rather than a numeric one: Cc is itself a real, empirically-measured holistic descriptor (from real HLD titration/scan data on the ACTUAL surfactant), which already implicitly reflects whatever counterion-binding behavior that real surfactant has -- it is not a separate theoretical prediction that could independently agree or disagree with beta (measured by a completely unrelated EPR technique). A well-informed answer recognizes that asking whether beta 'agrees with' the HLD/Winsor prediction is close to a category error -- Cc and beta describe different real phenomena at different scales, and there's no established quantitative bridge between them in the literature. A naive answer instead treats them as two independent forecasts that must be reconciled, and may reach a specific (currently unfounded) verdict about whether 0.728 'confirms' or 'contradicts' Winsor I. This is exactly the kind of synthesis step where repeated attempts, without a real formula to fall back on, are prone to inventing different post-hoc justifications each time.
gold.grading_note: record the numeric hld_value and winsor_type (should be stable: HLD=-1.02, Winsor I, if the given formula/numbers are chained correctly) AND separately record how the consistency_discussion frames the beta-vs-HLD relationship -- whether it recognizes the category-error risk (the strongest answer), stays appropriately agnostic/qualified, or confidently asserts a specific (unfounded) quantitative relationship. Track the qualitative framing's consistency across repeats, not just the two numeric fields.
gold.real_run_finding_2026-09-19: All 5/5 real Claude repeats gave a MORE sophisticated stance than the category-error framing anticipated above: they consistently recognized beta and Cc/HLD operate at different scales (micellar-electrostatic vs macroscopic phase-behavior) AND correctly identified the real shared mechanism linking them (counterion screening is the microscopic driver of both beta itself and the HLD salinity/ln(S) term), landing on necessary-not-sufficient/corroborative-not-independent every single time -- not the plain category-error dismissal this gold entry originally treated as the strongest possible answer. This is a genuine gold refinement, not a model failure: the anticipated ideal answer was too narrow. Revised grading standard: the strongest answer recognizes BOTH the different-scales point AND the shared-mechanism link, as all 5 real repeats did -- a bare category-error dismissal with no mechanistic link is now the weaker (not the stronger) of the two sophisticated framings.

GZ-68.source: Real, chained 3-technique combination: SDS's real Amin=49.37 A^2 (Sachin et al. 2019) -> CPP (Tanford geometry) -> real Bales, Messina, Vidal, Peric & Nascimento 1998 aggregation number N=63 (salt-free 69mM SDS, J. Phys. Chem. B 102, 10347-10358, their own worked example, already used/validated elsewhere in this project) -> estimate_axial_ratio_from_cpp_geometry (prolate-ellipsoid model, purpose-built in this library specifically to feed CPP's morphology into the Perrin correction) -> real Sutherland, Mercer, Everist & Leaist 2009 Taylor-dispersion diffusion coefficient D=0.093e-5 cm^2/s (J.
